motivation: The primary matched-risk-set test showed that durable extinctions occur in smaller colony codes. This audit asks whether that ordering is more size-selective than expected from the trivial fact that small counts have a higher probability of reaching zero under proportional stochastic thinning.
scope: Mechanism falsification audit; not an independent confirmatory test because the primary extinction result is already known.
risk_sets: Use the exact event-bearing island-year risk sets and durable-extinction labels from PALMER_COLONY_EXTINCTION_HAZARD_V1, excluding risk sets with fewer than two at-risk colonies or no survivor comparator.

common_rate.definition: For each risk set, r_t = sum(next-year counts over the same prior-positive at-risk colony codes) / sum(prior counts over those codes).
common_rate.role: Conditions on the shared island-year demographic change experienced by the risk set.

conditional_event_identity_null.conditioning: Within each risk set preserve the observed number k of durable extinctions.
conditional_event_identity_null.subset_probability: Under independent Bernoulli zero probabilities q_j, conditional on exactly k events, a candidate event subset S has probability proportional to product_{j in S} q_j/(1-q_j).
conditional_event_identity_null.implementation: Enumerate all k-subsets exactly within each risk set, normalize their weights, then Monte Carlo sample one subset per risk set.

statistic: The same equal-risk-set-weighted event-minus-survivor standardized log1p prior-size contrast as the primary hazard contract.
tail: one-sided probability that the zero-boundary null statistic is <= the observed statistic, with +1 Monte Carlo correction.

decision.exceeds_zero_boundary: Observed contrast < 0 and p <= 0.05 under all three zero models.
decision.size_selection_only: Primary exchangeability test is supported but one or more zero-boundary models have p > 0.05.
decision.interpretation: Only exceeds_zero_boundary permits saying size-selective disappearance is stronger than expected from proportional stochastic zero-hitting alone.

boundaries: Even if the audit is passed, do not identify skua predation or social facilitation as the unique cause.
If the audit fails, retain the descriptive result that durable extinctions occur from small colony codes, but do not present the size effect itself as evidence for an Allee/social mechanism.
Do not tune the common-rate definition, CV values, tail, or event conditioning after null results are opened.
